answers.answer: To describe the person who invoked the command, use {user} for their name and the user. form of every other helper: {user.name} or {user.login} for the login, {user.subject}, {user.object}, {user.possessive}, {user.tense} and {user.verb:<sing|plur>} for pronouns and grammar, and {user.points}, {user.followAge} and the {user.stats.*} and {viewer.*} helpers for their stats. Arguments go inside the braces: {user.verb:plays|play} takes the singular and plural verb forms, and {user.data.<key>} takes a key with an optional default after a colon.
answers.quote: Type the user. form, such as {user.subject}, to always get the person who used the command.

answers.answer: You need a trigger that supplies a person. Without one, a {user.*} helper stays in the reply as written. Event-specific helpers need their event. Viewer-written text is also governed by the Viewer Templates setting and permissions. Each table's Use in column says which template fields accept the helper. Points come from the bot's channel currency, not Twitch Channel Points.
answers.quote: A pipeline still needs a trigger that supplies the relevant person, message, or event; event-specific helpers need that event.

answers.answer: The user. helpers always describe the person who used the command. The bare helpers {name}, {link}, {subject}, {object}, {possessive}, {tense}, {presentTense}, {genderedTerm} and {verb:...} describe the first word typed after the command. They fall back to the caller only when nothing follows the command. Success is a reply that names the right person: in {user} sends a hug to {target.displayname}, the caller and the named person stay distinct.
answers.quote: They are about the person the command names, which is the first word after the command, as in !hug @someone.

answers.answer: When a viewer types !hug @someone, {user}, {user.name}, {user.subject}, {user.possessive}, {user.verb:...} and the other user. and viewer. helpers still describe the invoking viewer. {name}, {link}, {subject}, {object}, {possessive}, {tense}, {presentTense}, {genderedTerm} and {verb:...} switch to @someone, because the bot treats the first word after the command as the person named. Even !lurk getting food names getting, so a reply about the caller must use the user. form.
answers.quote: If nothing is typed after the command, they are about the person who used the command.
